shared_elements: row of short parallel vertical strokes (comb-like band)
justification: Both surfaces distribute small profile animals, humanoid figures and rows of short parallel strokes across a stone face, and both organise some motifs into loose horizontal registers, which is the most specific correspondence. But A is a tall, three-dimensional bas-relief on a shaped upright block with modelled, volumetric bodies, whereas B is a flat expanse of ground rock bearing thin, silhouetted, monochrome outline figures scattered with much empty space, so the manner of rendering and the overall format have almost nothing in common.
